common_name: Flare Hardy Hibiscus (Cherry-Pink Flaring-Flower Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: A refined, clump-forming hardy hibiscus, Flare opens huge flaring flowers in bright cherry-pink to fuchsia-red, often reaching ten inches across, against neat apple-green foliage rather than the darker leaves typical of many hardy hibiscus cultivars. Its recognition through the Texas Superstar program reflects strong heat and humidity tolerance across a range of soil types, including alkaline ground. Grow it in full sun with steady moisture; like other hardy hibiscus it dies back completely each winter and re-emerges later than most perennials in spring.
sources: Texas Superstar Program (Texas A&M AgriLife Extension)

common_name: Blue River Hardy Hibiscus (White Dinner-Plate Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Predating the larger-flowered 'Blue River II,' this older hardy hibiscus selection bears pure white, ten-inch flowers over a mounding clump of maple-shaped green leaves. It stays somewhat more compact than its later namesake, typically reaching four to five feet tall with a narrower spread. Full sun and reliably moist to wet soil keep it blooming heavily from midsummer into fall, and like all hardy hibiscus it dies to the ground each winter and emerges late in spring.

common_name: Pink Clouds Hardy Hibiscus (Deep Pink Giant-Flower Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: This heavy-blooming hardy hibiscus produces intensely deep pink flowers up to ten inches wide over bold, maple-like foliage, reaching roughly five feet tall from a dormant crown each season. It flowers prolifically from midsummer into fall and tends to break dormancy later in spring than most other perennials, so mark its location to avoid disturbing new shoots. Full sun and rich, evenly moist soil produce the best bloom, and established clumps tolerate occasional standing water.

common_name: Cherry Brandy Hardy Hibiscus (Compact Rosy-Red Cordial-Series Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Part of the compact Cordial series bred for smaller gardens, Cherry Brandy carries large, rounded, rosy-red flowers above bold, broad leaves on a noticeably shorter and fuller plant than standard hardy hibiscus. Its tidy, well-branched habit suits containers and smaller borders where full-size cultivars would overwhelm the space. Give it full sun and consistently moist soil, and expect the top growth to die back completely each winter.

common_name: Cinnamon Grappa Hardy Hibiscus (Dark-Foliage Cranberry-Red Cordial-Series Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: A sibling to 'Cherry Brandy' in the dwarf Cordial series, Cinnamon Grappa pairs oversized, plush cranberry-red flowers with leaves cast in a deep, smoky bronze that darkens as the season progresses. Like other Cordial introductions it stays noticeably shorter and fuller than standard hardy hibiscus cultivars, making it a good fit for smaller sunny beds. It flowers from midsummer into early fall and needs steady moisture through the growing season to support its oversized blooms.

common_name: Watermelon Ruffles Hardy Hibiscus (Ruffled Magenta-Pink Summerific Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: A Summerific-series selection, Watermelon Ruffles produces heavily ruffled, puckered magenta-pink flowers more than eight inches across on a vigorous clump reaching four to five feet tall. The crinkled petal texture sets it apart from smoother-flowered hardy hibiscus and draws steady pollinator traffic through summer. Plant in full sun with consistently moist soil, and cut the dead stalks down in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Peppermint Flare Hardy Hibiscus (White Speckled Pink Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Introduced by Texas horticulturist Greg Grant, Peppermint Flare bears huge white flowers, often nine inches across, flecked and brushed irregularly with pink-purple rather than carrying a single solid color. The plant forms a cold-hardy clump of green deciduous foliage and flowers continuously from summer into fall. Grow it in full sun with steady moisture, and expect it to die back completely each winter before returning later than most perennials in spring.

common_name: Red River Hardy Hibiscus (Wine-Red White-Throated Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Red River bears large, cup-shaped, wine-red flowers set off by a contrasting white-marked throat, blooming on an upright clump from midsummer through early fall. It shares the extreme cold hardiness and wetland tolerance typical of hardy hibiscus, thriving in rain gardens and pond margins as well as well-watered borders. Full sun and consistently moist to wet soil produce the heaviest flowering, and the plant dies back completely each winter, emerging later than most perennials in spring.

common_name: Carousel Red Wine Hardy Hibiscus (Dark Purple-Foliage Red Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Carousel Red Wine carries huge dark red flowers with a bright yellow central throat, each bloom reaching six to seven inches across, set against sharply cut, near-black purple leaves that add contrast even between flushes of bloom. The plant forms a compact, bushy, woody-based clump that stays shorter than many dinner-plate hardy hibiscus cultivars. Plant in full sun with reliably moist soil, and cut the top growth back hard in late winter since it regrows from the base each spring.

common_name: Carousel Pink Candy Hardy Hibiscus (Dark-Eyed Light Pink Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: A sibling selection in the Carousel series, Pink Candy opens bold, rounded, light pink flowers with a darker pink center, pale overtones, and a dark red eye ringed by creamy white anthers, each bloom six to seven inches wide. Its sharply cut, near-black purple leaves echo the rest of the Carousel line and contrast strongly with the pastel blooms. Full sun and consistent moisture support heavy flowering from late summer into fall, and the plant dies back to the ground each winter.

common_name: Carousel Giant Red Hardy Hibiscus (Large Red-Flower Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Carousel Giant Red produces large red flowers on the same deeply dissected, dark-foliaged framework shared by its Carousel-series siblings 'Red Wine' and 'Pink Candy.' It forms a compact, well-branched clump and blooms from summer into fall. Grow it in full sun with steady moisture, and expect the plant to die back completely each winter before re-emerging later than most perennials in spring.
